newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: Arab fund, ATFP extend $25mln in loans to Jordan.
newsitem.headline: Arab fund, ATFP extend $25mln in loans to Jordan.

text.p: The Arab Monetary Fund (AMF) said on Monday it and the Arab Trade Financing Programme (ATFP) had signed three agreements extending loans worth $25 million to Jordan.
"The loans are aimed at helping Jordan to finance the deficit in its 1996 balance of payments," an AMF statement said.
The agreements were signed by Jordan's Central Bank Governor Ziyad Fariz and AMF and ATFP chairman Jassim al-Manai.
The Abu Dhabi-based AMF -- the Arab world's premier finacial institution -- was set up by 20 Arab governments in 1977 to lay foundations for Arab integration and promote economic development.
ATFP is 50 percent owned by the AMF and other institutions.
